analysis: Exploratory: do newer-generation LLM judges change the judge-disagreement null? Same committed rows, same J1 prompt (problem statement + final diff), two additional judges from a different model generation.
reading: Individual judges improve markedly with model generation: gpt-6-sol reaches 0.776 [0.68, 0.87] on the larger sample, the best single detector anywhere in this study, and gpt-6-luna and gpt-6-sol both beat every gpt-5 judge on both benchmarks. Their disagreement does not improve - it is 0.41 on both benchmarks, below the 0.51-0.53 of the weaker gpt-5 trio. The five-judge panel gives 0.62 on 12 positives and 0.44 on 35. Better critics, no better disagreement.
caveats: The gpt-6 panel has only two members, so its disagreement is a single absolute difference and a weaker statistic than a four-member spread; the five-judge row is the fair panel comparison.
Exploratory, not pre-registered. Ten quantities per benchmark, no multiplicity correction.
Single-vendor still: all five judges are OpenAI models, so shared-blind-spot concerns are not retired.
why_it_matters: It retires the objection that the judge-disagreement null reflects weak judges. The dissociation between what critics know individually and what their disagreement conveys now holds across two model generations, and widens as the critics get better.
